correctness.rationale: Strict negative-definite Hessian from the unrolled positive exponential interval sum proves unique global maximum. The final visit must be at the season end and the first visit cannot be at time zero, since replacing a zero-time pass with a deadline pass strictly improves the count. Adjoint gradients p U_i Q_i and adjacent KKT equalities force equal pre-search stocks and identical middle gaps. The unique monotone scalar root yields all gaps and collision threshold, with boundary equality treated exactly and subthreshold maximum uniquely on simplex boundary. Standalone checker.py passed 15,020 deterministic and exact-rational diagnostics; no finite experiment substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2011 and 2015 primary carcass-search articles, inspected full text of Wolpert 2015 and related indexed ecological sampling results do not establish the exact arbitrary-n global maximizer, its concavity proof, the endpoint offset log(1/p)/lambda, or h_c=(n-2)log(2-p)-log p. Wolpert supplies a model more general than the detection-count process, but his mortality estimator formulas are not an implication of its optimal calendar. Full Etterson (2013) text was inaccessible: historical priority qualified, not independently certified.
residual_risks: Full text of Etterson (2013) remains unavailable; its irregular-interval analysis and possible appendices could affect priority.
A pre-existing inspection-design theorem in unindexed operations-research literature could imply the maximization after an appropriate model reduction.
Generality of the known mortality-estimation equations is acknowledged: only exact global optimization and sharp transition are claimed as apparently new.

value.rationale: Repeated carcass searches under nonzero scavenging and imperfect detection are a well-motivated wildlife-mortality monitoring problem. The result gives an exact global n-visit search calendar, sharp threshold between fully separated and coincident surveys, and a universal first/last offset independent of visit count or season length. It distinguishes maximization of discovered counts from mortality-estimator accuracy and exposes the cost of equal spacing in a physically interpretable benchmark. The model is deliberately simplified and is not presented as real-world monitoring advice.
